text: # Finance Billing & Dispute Policy ## Transaction Disputes Customers may dispute transactions within 60 days of posting date. Required information: account number, transaction ID, and dispute reason. ## Billing Discrepancies Common causes: duplicate charges, incorrect tax application, currency conversion errors. Resolution SLA: 5 business days for routine cases. ## Reconciliation Status Monthly reconciliation closes on the 3rd business day. Status inquiries require account number and statement period (YYYY-MM). ## Payment Delays Payment delays beyond 30 days trigger escalation to collections. Customers should provide payment reference and expected settlement date. ## Escalation Criteria Escalate to human analyst when: amount exceeds
$50,000, regulatory complaint mentioned, fraud suspected, or customer requests supervisor.

# Dispute Resolution Runbook ## Routine Query Resolution 1. Verify account and transaction in SQL Server ledger. 2. Check posting date and settlement status. 3. Respond with policy-aligned timeline and next steps. ## Complex Case Escalation Pre-populate case summary with: intent, extracted entities, RAG context snippets, account snapshot. ## Compliance Language Always include: "This response is informational and does not constitute legal advice." ## Response Boundaries Do not promise refunds. Do not share other customers' data. Do not override audit holds without analyst approval.
